sophia: quick alert — bringing up sybil-int6 for code+docs retrieval. saw a sharp drop for CODE queries at R@5 but docs look fine. attaching short run.
sophia: command I ran:
```
./emb_bench --model=sybil-int6 --dataset=code_docs_holdout_2k --split=code,docs --k=1,5 --quant=per-tensor --whiten=global --batch=128
```
kai: paste table pls. small threads = fast fix :)
sophia: small table (avg 3 runs):
```
model        split  R@1    R@5
sybil-fp16   code   0.512  0.682
sybil-int6   code   0.498  0.591  <-- big R@5 drop
sybil-fp16   docs   0.537  0.704
sybil-int6   docs   0.532  0.699
```
noah: interesting that top1 is stable for code but R@5 collapsed. suggests nearest-neighbor neighborhood gets scrambled further down. maybe tokenizer/subword effects for code tokens after quant.
sophia: I checked embedding norm stats by split:
```
metric  model      split  mean_norm  std
L2      sybil-fp16 code   11.9       1.8
L2      sybil-int6 code   11.2       4.0   <-- heavy tail
L2      sybil-fp16 docs   12.4       1.9
L2      sybil-int6 docs   12.3       2.1
```
kai: heavy tail only for code. Code tokens have many short unique identifiers -> rare token space. Calibration sampling might have under-sampled code lexemes. Try calibration with code-augmented sample and per-channel quant.
sophia: queued two runs: (A) stratified calib including code tokens (6301234600), (B) per-channel int6 (6301234700).
bench-bot: run 6301234600 done: sybil-int6-code-augcalib R@5 = 0.639 (improved). logs: /bench/6301234600/log.txt
bench-bot: run 6301234700 done: sybil-int6-perchan R@5 = 0.678 (near fp16).
noah: per-channel wins. aug-calib helps a lot too. hypothesis: quant noise + whitening trained mostly on docs pushes code vectors into denser doc neighborhoods, hurting mid-ranked recall.
kai: next steps: (1) update onboarding checklist to require domain-aware calibration sampling when model targets mixed domains (code/docs), (2) prefer per-channel quant for code-capable models, (3) add microbench that reports R@k per-domain and L2 tail stats + top1-top5 cosine-gap.
sophia: opening PR with checklist edits, bench flags, and a canary rule: fail int6 if any domain's R@5 drops >0.04 vs fp16. will also add a short note in model card about tokenization sparsity for code.
noah: good. also add a small tokenizer-coverage check for rare byte sequences when onboarding code models.
kai: thanks team "
